input.text:
Grandma Ruth's Banana Bread

Prep time: 15 minutes · Bake time: 55 minutes · Total time: 1 hour 10 minutes
Makes one 9 x 5 inch loaf (10 slices)

Ingredients
- 3 very ripe bananas, mashed
- 1/3 cup melted butter
- 3/4 cup brown sugar
- 1 egg, beaten
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
- 1 teaspoon baking soda
- a pinch of salt
- 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour

Method
1. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and butter a loaf pan.
2. Stir the melted butter into the mashed bananas, then mix in the sugar, egg and vanilla.
3. Sprinkle the baking soda and salt over the mixture and stir. Fold in the flour until just combined.
4. Pour into the pan and bake for 55 to 60 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
5. Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack.

Ruth's note from 1987: it is even better the next day, toasted with salted butter.

Brainstorm: onboarding experience for new customers
Date: March 3rd, 2026
Participants: Grace Liu, Mateo Alvarez, Hiroshi Tanaka, Chloe Martin

We spent the hour throwing around ideas; nothing was decided.

- Grace thinks the welcome email is too long and that a three-step checklist inside the product might work better. Mateo was not convinced and pointed out that the last in-product checklist we tried had a 9% completion rate.
- Hiroshi floated the idea of a 15-minute onboarding call for accounts above 50 seats. Someone should probably check whether support has the capacity for that, but it is not clear who.
- Chloe shared three competitor onboarding flows she had screenshotted. People liked the progress bar in one of them.
- We talked about extending the trial from 14 to 21 days. Opinions were split, and we agreed it needs data before anyone argues for it.
- Mateo mentioned that the pricing page redesign (shipped 2026-02-17) may already have changed who signs up, which would make any comparison with last quarter tricky.

Parking lot: localisation of the onboarding emails; a "getting started" video.

We will pick this up again at the same time next week, with the goal of choosing two ideas to prototype.

input.text:
Product & Engineering leadership meeting
Thursday 8 October 2026, 10:00 to 11:30, Room Atlas and video

Attendees: Rebecca Holm (chair), Samuel Adeyemi, Yuki Watanabe, Carlos Mendes, Fatima Zahra
Apologies: Peter Novak (on leave until 19 October)
Notes taken by Yuki

1. Q4 roadmap check-in
Rebecca reviewed the Q4 roadmap. Of the nine committed items, five are on track, three are at risk and one (bulk export) has been cut and moved to Q1. The at-risk items are the new permissions model, the audit log and the Android widget. Samuel said the permissions model is blocked on a design decision about inherited roles; the team has two options and needs a call this month.

2. Vendor contract for the observability platform
Carlos reported on the renewal. The vendor's initial quote was $84,000 a year for the expanded plan. After two rounds of negotiation we agreed on $71,500 a year with a two-year term and a 5% cap on the second-year increase. Finance has seen the numbers and is comfortable. The contract still needs a signature from legal.

3. Hiring
Fatima shared the pipeline: two senior backend offers are out, one accepted (start date 2 November 2026) and one pending. The data engineer role has had few qualified applicants; Fatima suggested widening the search to remote candidates in the EU, and the group agreed.

4. Incident review
Yuki summarised the 29 September outage: a certificate expired on an internal service and took down login for 47 minutes. The fix is in place, but certificate expiry is still monitored by hand. Everyone agreed this needs automating before the end of the quarter.

5. Android widget
Samuel and Yuki disagree on whether to ship a reduced version of the widget in Q4 or move the whole thing to Q1. No decision today; Rebecca asked for a one-page comparison so the group can decide at the next meeting.

6. Any other business
Carlos mentioned that the office network upgrade is scheduled for the weekend of 24 October 2026 and that no one in this group needs to do anything for it. Fatima reminded everyone that the performance review cycle opens on 2 November 2026; managers will receive the forms by email from the people team. Rebecca thanked Yuki for the clear incident write-up.

Decisions
- Bulk export moves to Q1.
- The observability contract goes ahead at the agreed $71,500 a year.
- The data engineer search is widened to remote EU candidates.

Action items
- Samuel: write up the two inherited-roles options with a recommendation, by 15 October 2026.
- Carlos: get the observability contract signed by legal, by 16 October 2026.
- Fatima: update the data engineer job posting for remote EU candidates (no deadline set).
- Yuki: set up automated certificate-expiry alerts for all internal services, by 30 October 2026.
- Samuel: one-page comparison of the two widget options, by 21 October 2026.

Next meeting: Thursday 22 October 2026, same time.
